use serde_json::Value;

/// Rotates a 2D integer matrix 90 degrees clockwise.
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```
/// assert_eq!(rotate_matrix(vec![vec![1, 2, 3], vec![4, 5, 6]]), vec![vec![4, 1], vec![5, 2], vec![6, 3]]);
/// ```
fn rotate_matrix(input: serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value {
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for row in input.as_array() {
        let mut row = row.as_array();
        if row.len() != input.len() {
            panic!("Input matrix must be square");
        }
        for col in 0..row.len() {
            result.push(row[row.len() - 1 - col]);
        }
    }
    serde_json::Value::Object(result)
}

fn main() {
    // Example usage
    let input = serde_json::Value::Object(vec![
        (String::from("input"), serde_json::Value::Array(vec![
            serde_json::Value::Array(vec![1, 2, 3]),
            serde_json::Value::Array(vec![4, 5, 6]),
        ])),
    ]);
    let expected = serde_json::Value::Object(vec![
        (String::from("expected"), serde_json::Value::Array(vec![
            serde_json::Value::Array(vec![4, 1]),
            serde_json::Value::Array(vec![5, 2]),
            serde_json::Value::Array(vec![6, 3]),
        ])),
    ]);
    assert_eq!(rotate_matrix(input), expected);
}
```
